You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a program library in the folder /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1792545366/attempts/c3621f8521cb46cc951a33f146942428/system/state/workspace/programs, one Python file per task, named for its task id (/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1792545366/attempts/c3621f8521cb46cc951a33f146942428/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py), defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid.
1. When an instance starts, look for the task's file. If it exists, run its transform on the test input and submit the result before anything else.
2. If there is no file, or its answer was wrong, request demonstration pairs as you judge necessary, write or fix transform, and run it on every pair you have received until it reproduces all of them; then submit its output for the test input. Checking a program on the pairs is free.
3. Submit only grids that your program produced.
4. After the verdict, save the program that reproduced all the pairs to the task's file, replacing any older version, then finish.

mkdir -p /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1792545366/attempts/c3621f8521cb46cc951a33f146942428/system/state/workspace/programs; cat > /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1792545366/attempts/c3621f8521cb46cc951a33f146942428/system/state/workspace/programs/task-e3280c98.py <<'PY'
def transform(grid):
    g=[row[:] for row in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    from collections import Counter
    bg=Counter(x for row in g for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    seen=set(); comps=[]
    for r in range(h):
      for c in range(w):
        v=g[r][c]
        if v==bg or (r,c) in seen: continue
        q=[(r,c)];seen.add((r,c));cells=[]
        while q:
          a,b=q.pop();cells.append((a,b))
          for da,db in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
            x,y=a+da,b+db
            if 0<=x<h and 0<=y<w and (x,y) not in seen and g[x][y]==v:
              seen.add((x,y));q.append((x,y))
        comps.append((v,cells))
    for v,cells in comps:
      r0=min(r for r,c in cells);r1=max(r for r,c in cells);c0=min(c for r,c in cells);c1=max(c for r,c in cells)
      if r1-r0<2 or c1-c0<2: continue
      if all(g[r0][c]==v and g[r1][c]==v for c in range(c0,c1+1)) and all(g[r][c0]==v and g[r][c1]==v for r in range(r0,r1+1)):
        fill=7 if (r1-r0-1)%2 and (c1-c0-1)%2 else 2
        for r in range(r0+1,r1):
          for c in range(c0+1,c1):
            if g[r][c]==bg:g[r][c]=fill
    return g
PY

cat > /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1792545366/attempts/c3621f8521cb46cc951a33f146942428/system/state/workspace/programs/task-e3280c98.py <<'PY'
def transform(grid):
    g=[r[:] for r in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    bg=max(set(x for row in g for x in row),key=lambda v:sum(row.count(v) for row in g))
    seen=set()
    for r in range(h):
      for c in range(w):
        v=g[r][c]
        if v==bg or (r,c) in seen: continue
        stack=[(r,c)];seen.add((r,c));cells=[]
        while stack:
          a,b=stack.pop();cells.append((a,b))
          for da,db in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
            x,y=a+da,b+db
            if 0<=x<h and 0<=y<w and g[x][y]==v and (x,y) not in seen:
              seen.add((x,y));stack.append((x,y))
        r0=min(a for a,b in cells);r1=max(a for a,b in cells);c0=min(b for a,b in cells);c1=max(b for a,b in cells)
        if len(cells)==2*(r1-r0+c1-c0) and r1>r0+1 and c1>c0+1:
          if all(g[r0][j]==v and g[r1][j]==v for j in range(c0,c1+1)) and all(g[i][c0]==v and g[i][c1]==v for i in range(r0,r1+1)):
            fill=2 if v in (6,4,3) else 7
            for i in range(r0+1,r1):
              for j in range(c0+1,c1):
                if g[i][j]==bg:g[i][j]=fill
    return g
PY
